selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What two things does the passage say are necessary for the ruler’s goals in the palace to be fulfilled?
questions.answer: The teacher must be present, and the people must accept his guidance and act on it.

questions.question: Why is the teacher’s presence presented as essential?
questions.answer: Without someone to explain the meaning and purpose of the palace, its message would remain unclear and its goals would fail.

questions.question: What comparison is used to show why a teacher is needed?
questions.answer: A difficult book without an instructor is compared to something that has no meaningful benefit because no one can understand it.

questions.question: According to the passage, how is the teacher connected to the palace’s existence?
questions.answer: His presence is described as a reason the palace was built at all.

questions.question: How are the people’s response to the teacher and the palace’s continuation connected?
questions.answer: The palace continues in its intended state only if people listen to the teacher and follow his instruction.

questions.question: What is expected to happen if the people ignore the teacher’s guidance?
questions.answer: The palace will definitely be altered and no longer remain as it was.

questions.question: In this passage, what are the two foundations for the success of the palace’s purpose?
questions.answer: One is the existence of the master, and the other is the people’s acceptance of what he says.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the result of having no master?
questions.answer: It says the whole effort would lose its purpose because no one would be able to understand what everything means.

questions.question: Why does the passage bring up the example of a book that cannot be understood?
questions.answer: To show that even something valuable becomes useless if there is no one to explain it.

questions.question: What role do the people play in relation to the palace’s future?
questions.answer: Their listening and obedience help keep the palace in its proper form and purpose.

questions.question: If the people refuse to listen, what does the passage say will happen with certainty?
questions.answer: The palace will be changed and transformed.

questions.question: In what sense are the people’s actions called a cause of the palace’s continuation?
questions.answer: Their hearing and obeying the master are what allow the palace to remain meaningful and endure in its intended way.

questions.question: What does the speaker say the listener has already understood about the palace?
questions.answer: That the ruler built it for the purposes mentioned earlier in the story.

questions.question: What does the passage say those purposes depend on?
questions.answer: They depend on the presence of the master and on people accepting his words.

questions.question: Why would the ruler’s aims become pointless without the master?
questions.answer: Because no one would be able to grasp the meaning of the palace and what it was meant to show.

questions.question: What does the image of unreadable writing teach in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches that meaning is not enough by itself; it must also be explained so that people can understand it.

questions.question: In what sense is the master called a cause of the palace?
questions.answer: He is so important to its purpose that the passage speaks as if the palace would not even have been built without him.

questions.question: What final outcome is mentioned if people do not pay attention to the master’s instruction?
questions.answer: The palace will be transformed with certainty.

questions.question: Which two conditions are named as necessary for the ruler’s goals to be achieved?
questions.answer: The first is that the master exists, and the second is that the people listen to him and accept his teaching.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by comparing the situation to a difficult text without a teacher?
questions.answer: Something full of meaning may still seem empty if no one can explain it.

questions.question: Why is the master more than just a helpful addition in the story?
questions.answer: He is presented as necessary to the whole purpose of the palace, not merely as an extra benefit.

questions.question: Why is listening to the master not treated as a minor matter?
questions.answer: Because the survival of the palace’s intended order is tied to whether people respond to him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the palace if people fail to listen?
questions.answer: It says the palace will certainly be changed into something else.

questions.question: According to the passage, what are the two main requirements for the palace’s aims to be realized?
questions.answer: There must be a master to explain things, and the people must receive and follow his explanation.

title: Secret of the Parable Presence of the Master and Acceptance of His Word
